title: 19.4 An 8.1-to-9.9GHz Single-Core Pseudo-Series-Resonance Oscillator Achieving -128.7dBc/Hz PN at 1MHz
problem: Achieving ultra-low phase noise in CMOS oscillators is limited by resonator Q-factor; coupled multi-core architectures theoretically reduce phase noise by 10log(N) but suffer from core mismatches and area overhead. Series-resonance (SR) oscillators promise single-core ultra-low PN but require either bipolar technology with diodes or four-stage inverter chains burning >300 mW.
motivation: Ultra-low phase-noise oscillators are prerequisites for high-order modulation and high-throughput 5G-Advanced/6G communications; achieving this in standard CMOS with minimal power enables more efficient frequency synthesizers.
method: A pseudo-series-resonance (PSR) CMOS oscillator that achieves series-resonance phase-noise benefits without the power overhead of four-stage inverter designs. The design employs a novel cross-coupled core topology providing current-controlled negative resistance suitable for CMOS, feeding into LC resonators that provide low-noise oscillation.
key_novelty: First practical single-core CMOS series-resonance oscillator achieving -128.7 dBc/Hz phase noise at 1 MHz offset with minimal power (sub-300 mW), eliminating multi-core area and mismatch penalties.
contributions: Pseudo-series-resonance topology enabling series-resonance benefits in standard CMOS
Novel cross-coupled core providing current-controlled negative resistance
Ultra-low phase noise (-128.7 dBc/Hz @ 1 MHz) with single-core efficiency
8.1–9.9 GHz tuning range practical for 5G/6G communications
limitations: Power consumption, FoM, and 1/f³ PN corner not specified in abstract; full tuning range not detailed.
primary_theme: Single-core series-resonance CMOS oscillator with ultra-low phase noise for 5G/6G
